diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Today, several forcibly retired faculty members of Farhangian University protested in front of the Ministry of Education. They say that despite parliamentary commissions' emphasis on continuing their service, no effective action has been taken to resolve their issue. Over 320 faculty members were forcibly retired last year and have not received their salaries.

Mohammad Khatami stated that the Islamic Republic has imposed its survival and existence on the enemy after the war. He called for avoiding tension and adhering to the agreement to preserve Iran's dignity. Khatami described honorable peace as the solution and emphasized that life with war is impossible.

In recent weeks, several drones have entered the airspace of European countries. A drone made by the Islamic Republic was shot down in Romania, and a Spanish F-18 fighter also shot down a drone in Romanian airspace. This issue has raised concerns about increasing tensions between Russia and NATO.

Jared Kushner, senior advisor to Donald Trump, called Egypt a key partner of the US in the Middle East and praised its role in efforts for peace and stability. Kushner and Sisi met in El Alamein to discuss Middle East developments, the Palestinian issue, and the implementation of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza. Sisi called for continued cooperation to address regional challenges.

Romania announced the downing of a drone in its airspace early Sunday, August 16. The drone entered Romania from Moldova and was shot down by a Spanish F-18 fighter jet. The Spanish fighter was on a NATO air patrol mission.

The Supreme Court overturned the death sentences of Shahab Zahdi, Abolfazl Salehi Siavashani, and Yaser Rajaifar. These individuals were sentenced to death in connection with the fire at a Basij base. Their case has been referred back to the Tehran Revolutionary Court for retrial.

Amir Hatami, the commander-in-chief of the Islamic Republic of Iran's army, announced that any army personnel who kills or captures an "American force" will receive a $30,000 reward. He added that the reward for killing or capturing American female forces would be double, approximately 11.2 billion tomans.

Hossein Samsami stated that the government is implementing policies that led to the protests in January 2026, with the parliament also involved. He warned these policies will increase budget deficits and inflation in the long term. Samsami criticized the ration card policy and the official exchange rate increase, and called medicalian's statements about currency shortages incorrect.

Amid a deadlock in negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic, Washington has expanded its diplomatic consultations to European allies including Austria and Greece. This was discussed in an interview with Ali Hassanpour, a reporter for Iran International.

The US Department of War has asked major arms manufacturers to present specific plans to increase ammunition production capacity as quickly as possible. This request comes as the US battle against the Islamic Republic has put heavy pressure on reserves of some US air defense and missile defense ammunition, even more than the war in Ukraine.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced that three ships were attacked within 72 hours in the Strait of Hormuz. Two tankers were attacked on August 14 and one cargo ship on August 15. The organization did not provide details about the attackers or possible damages.

The head of Tehran's Management and Planning Organization reported a widespread shortage of urban and medical infrastructure. 32% of Tehran's population lives in worn-out areas and informal settlements. Tehran province faces a shortage of about 16,000 hospital beds and lacks infrastructure in various sectors.

A number of Afghans and civil activists gathered in Paris to protest against the Taliban's rule and the human rights situation in Afghanistan. The protesters emphasized the extensive restrictions on women and girls and the silence of the international community. A report and an interview with a women's rights activist were also presented.

The agreement between the US and the Islamic Republic expires on Monday, 26 Mordad, 60 days after signing. Tensions in the region continue with several attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz reported. Donald Trump stated that the US controls the passage of ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Esmail Hosseini from the Energy Commission of the Parliament said that damage to oil facilities and reduced production capacity will make managing gas shortages in the upcoming winter more difficult. He emphasized that gas shortages could affect fuel supply to power plants and the stability of the electricity network. If gas supply is insufficient, the use of liquid fuels such as gas oil and fuel oil will become necessary.

Ahmad Ariaee-Nejad, the representative of Malayer, described the death of Mahsa Amini with an insulting phrase and called the protests following her death "eight months of unrest." Mahsa Amini's parents considered these remarks offensive and responded strongly. They emphasized that such statements do not diminish their daughter's value and that her name will remain eternal in the country's history.

The Israeli army announced that on August 16, it targeted a member of Islamic Jihad in Khan Yunis and a member of Hamas in Nuseirat with airstrikes. These individuals were involved in planning attacks against Israel, according to the army. The Israeli army used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to minimize civilian harm.

The Iranian parliament has approved a bill criminalizing interviews and communication with foreign media, sending films and photos, scientific cooperation with some foreign universities, and cultural activities. The bill was approved with 183 votes in favor and requires Guardian Council approval to be enforced. Penalties include imprisonment from six months to five years and fines, with some terms in the bill left undefined.

Pezeshkian confirmed that with the naval blockade of Iran's ports and the halt of oil sales, gasoline prices must increase to 87,000 tomans. Islamic Republic officials attacked these statements and warned about people returning to the streets and repeating the 2019 protests. This report was prepared by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

A group of Iranians gathered near the Eiffel Tower in Paris to support political prisoners and demand an immediate release and halt to executions. They also called out the name of Reza Pahlavi as the leader of the transitional period. Participants urged increased international pressure on the Islamic Republic.

The Trump administration used Nechirvan Barzani to establish a direct channel with the IRGC command during secret negotiations with Iran to end the war. This was due to doubts about the authority of Iranian negotiators. The secret meeting in Erbil did not take place, but Barzani has expressed readiness to help resume negotiations.

The head of Alborz University of Medical Sciences reported the assault of four staff members at Shahid Madani Hospital in Karaj. The incident occurred after staff prevented relatives of a patient from entering the women's ward. Four main perpetrators of the clash have been arrested.

Cristiano Ronaldo stated in an interview that this year is likely his last year playing football and he wants to leave an extraordinary legacy. He also mentioned wanting to spend more time with his family and has planned for his future. Ronaldo emphasized the importance of filling time in various ways and enjoying life after football.

Don Bacon, a Republican congressman, stated that the US cannot allow the Islamic Republic to acquire nuclear weapons. He described a war with Iran as a "hard fight" and criticized Trump's communication about the war. Bacon also pointed to shortages in military weapons and called for greater transparency.

Arsenal won the 2026 Charity Shield by defeating Manchester City. Calafiori, Kai Havertz, and Odegaard scored for Arsenal. This is Arsenal's second trophy in four months and their eighteenth Charity Shield title.

The US government has sought help from Nechirvan Barzani to establish direct communication with the IRGC during negotiations with the Islamic Republic. Due to distrust in the positions of the Iranian negotiators, the Trump administration created a secret channel. Barzani plays a role similar to Qatar in mediating between the US and the Islamic Republic.

Arash Aramesh referred to Amir Hatami's statements about paying rewards for killing or capturing Americans. He said the Islamic Republic has a history of using proxy forces in the region. This call may be directed at groups and individuals willing to take hostages or kill Americans.

A prisoner named Kaveh Rafusheh was transferred to solitary confinement in Sanandaj prison for execution of the death sentence. He is 35 years old and from Sanandaj. The transfer took place today, Sunday, 25 Mordad.

Andrey Vorobyov, governor of Moscow region, stated that in a drone attack by Ukraine on the region, an 83-year-old man was killed and several people were injured. This attack was described as one of the largest on the Moscow region. A warehouse of Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, was targeted.

Younes Azadbar, a resident of Rasht, was arrested on Sunday, 25 Mordad, after a retirees' protest gathering. He was transferred to a detention center in the city. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Ali Motahari requested supervision of women's and men's clothing in the streets in a letter to Masoud Pezeshkian. He suggested that issues like revealing clothing and wearing leggings for women and shorts for men be monitored and discreetly warned. He also called for continued enforcement of dress regulations in government offices and universities.

Two young fans of the Tractor team died in a car accident on their way back to Bonab after the match against Paykan at Sahand Stadium in Tabriz. This news was announced by Hojat Karimi, the CEO of the Tractor club.

The 39th meeting of the heads of education across the country began on Sunday morning, 25th of Mordad, with a speech by Masoud Pezeshkian. During a segment called "Sports Bell," attendees performed physical exercises. Alireza Kazemi, the Minister of Education, was also present in this part.
A female blogger was arrested for posting a video considered insulting to sacred beliefs. A legal case has been filed against her. This incident occurred in cyberspace.

Faleh Sari, Iraq's finance minister, stated that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has directly impacted Iraq's economy. The Iraqi government seeks to increase non-oil revenues to reduce dependence on oil. There is also a plan to approve the first programmatic and performance budget in Iraq's history.

The US government used Nechirvan Barzani to establish a secret communication channel with the commander of the IRGC during negotiations with Tehran. Barzani contacted Ahmad Vahidi and learned about the IRGC's support for resolving the crisis through negotiation. This report was published by Axios citing informed sources.
Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said Washington is preparing to impose unprecedented economic pressure on Tehran.

Fatemeh Atashi Khiyavi, a political prisoner, was released from Evin Prison after completing her sentence. This news was reported by HRANA news agency. Her release occurred after the end of her imprisonment period.

The Lebanese army arrested four people in several operations across three cities on charges of arms and drug trafficking and possession of ammunition. One detainee is accused of forming a gang for trafficking war weapons. The army also seized drugs and equipment used to manufacture them.

Four of five defendants arrested during the January protests were executed less than three months later. Three of these defendants received death sentences without defense lawyers or visitation rights. Saeed Madani described this as a sign of serious decline in Iran and warned that without governance retreat, a violent revolution will occur.

Three workers died in the counties of Behbahan and Samalqan due to unsafe working conditions and lack of workplace safety. These incidents occurred while they were working. The report was published by Harana News Agency.

In the Titraval with Niousha Saremi, it was reported that the US has a direct channel with the IRGC through Barzani. The report mentions doubts about Qalibaf and approval from Vahidi. This topic was discussed in the audio version of Titraval.

Nechirvan Barzani, the president of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, is working to convey messages between the US and the Islamic Republic and reduce tensions. The Kurdistan Region has consistently emphasized resolving disputes through dialogue. Barzani's good relations with both sides are cited as the reason for his role.

Esmail Saghab Esfahani described Chinese-assembled cars in Iran as low quality and fuel-consuming. He said importing fully assembled Japanese cars would have been cheaper. He also noted that Iran's automotive industry is 60 years old.

With the end of the 60-day ceasefire between Iran and the US, Ahmad Vahidi stated he agrees with negotiating with the US to end the war. This news was reported by Axios. The discussion was with Farzin Nadimi at the Washington Institute.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad stated in the program "Cheshmandaz" that the plan to counter infiltration has no connection to combating espionage and continues previous approaches. He described the plan as a continuation of the approach used in the final years of Ali Khamenei's leadership under the term "infiltration." According to him, this plan imposes more restrictions on society.

The National Security Commission of the Parliament approved an article of the 'Tangsiri' law banning Israeli vessels from passing through the Persian Gulf. This approval is not the final ratification and requires confirmation from relevant authorities. If fully approved, Israeli vessels will not be allowed to transit the Persian Gulf.

Brad Cooper, the commander of US Central Command, stated that the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has one of the lowest mental health cases among active US Navy carriers. He praised the prioritization of crew mental health and resilience. Cooper also encouraged sailors and marines to continue their excellent work and wished them a smooth journey home.

Iranian users of the social network X have started a campaign by reposting the last posts of protesters who have not been online since January 8. The fate of these users is unclear, and it is possible they were killed or detained during the crackdown. This issue was reported by Aryan Risbaf.

Yadollah Javani, the political deputy of the IRGC, stated that the enemy cannot carry out surprise actions against Iran and should expect strategic surprises. He said the armed forces will take any necessary actions for defense and security at the right time. Javani also described current armed forces' actions as defensive and possibly becoming offensive in the future.

Delshad Shahab, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government, confirmed Nechirvan Barzani's role in conveying messages between Tehran and Washington and efforts to reduce tensions. Barzani emphasizes resolving differences through dialogue and maintaining the neutrality of the Kurdistan region. This approach has gained the trust of various parties.

Ahmadreza Alipour, a dismissed student of Tehran Central Azad University, was released from Tehran Grand Prison after completing his sentence. This release took place on Saturday, 24 Mordad 1405. Harana News Agency reported this news.
On Saturday, August 15, a military chase in Manoujan led to the overturning and burning of a fuel smuggler's vehicle. The driver died in the incident.

The parliament has passed a resolution to transform Iran into an Islamic North Korea. This topic was discussed in the audio version of Cheshmandaz. No further details about the resolution have been announced.

Lille defeated Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 to win the French Super Cup for the first time. The only goal was scored by Thauvin in the 32nd minute. The match had two red cards, and PSG failed to secure their 15th Super Cup title.

Al Arabiya reported that drones of Yemen's government forces targeted a gathering of Iran-backed Houthis in Al Aqsha area in Al Jawf province. The attack took place on the evening of Sunday, August 16. No further details were provided.

Persepolis football team won against Shams Azar in their first Premier League match in Qazvin. This was the first official game under the management of Mehdi Tartaar. Additionally, there was an interview with Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Iranian society is clearly divided into two poles. The majority wants the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, while a minority clings to power. He described this polarization as a prelude and necessity for the overthrow.

Donald Trump's representatives met with Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediators in Cairo to advance Trump's peace plan for Gaza. The talks took place while Israel continued airstrikes on the Gaza Strip. Kushner and Mladenov are scheduled to meet with the Israeli Prime Minister.

Morad Veysi, a senior analyst at Iran International, quoted Javidnam Mehdi Eskandarian saying he wanted to clarify his stance before becoming Javidnam. Veysi stated this is the most important question for every Iranian, to clarify their position towards the Islamic Republic. This position could be either overthrowing or preserving the Islamic Republic.

Donald Trump ordered a significant reduction in the scale of joint US-South Korea military exercises. He described these exercises as costly and sending a hostile message to North Korea. Trump also reported South Korea's refusal to join US efforts for the nuclear disarmament of the Islamic Republic.

The 60-day deadline in the memorandum of understanding between Tehran and Washington ends on Monday. Diplomatic efforts to reach a new agreement have made limited progress. Rising tensions in the region have posed serious obstacles to the talks.

Persepolis fans cheered Afshin Peyrovani during the match against Shams Azar. Mohsen Khalili, who replaced him, has stirred controversies around Persepolis. This issue was discussed in the Hattrick program with interviews by Mazdak Mirzaei.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that after 48 years, the people of Iran want the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. He added that people consider the promises of 1979 false and believe the rulers are unwilling to step down. He emphasized that the regime must be overthrown through a popular uprising.

The commander of the Iranian army announced a $30,000 reward for killing or capturing American soldiers. The amount will be doubled for female soldiers. Experts consider these statements a sign of confusion in the decision-making of the Islamic Republic's leaders.

Foreign ministers of several Arab and Islamic countries condemned Israel's opposition to Donald Trump's comprehensive plan to end the Gaza war. The plan was approved in UN Security Council resolution 2803. They stated that Israel's opposition is the main obstacle to peace efforts in Gaza and Palestine.

The commander of the US Central Command announced that the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier group is returning home after more than 260 days of mission in the Arabian Sea. The group shot down over 200 IRGC drones during operations against the Islamic Republic. The CENTCOM commander also mentioned the pressures of the long mission on the crew and their families.

The Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar emphasized the need for adherence to negotiation and diplomacy in a phone call with the Syrian Foreign Minister. They stressed ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and maintaining regional security. Qatar expressed full support for efforts to reduce tensions and achieve lasting peace.

Hamas called on mediator countries to compel Israel to implement the first phase of the Gaza ceasefire commitments after meeting with Jared Kushner. This request was made following talks in Cairo. Kushner is scheduled to meet Netanyahu to discuss stopping attacks and implementing the second phase of the agreement.

Anti-war protesters in South Korea gathered in front of the US embassy demanding the halt of the annual joint military exercise. The protest followed Trump's order to significantly reduce the scale of the exercises. The "Freedom Shield Ulchi" exercise with about 18,000 South Korean troops has started.

The Hengaw human rights organization reported that 16 people arrested in autumn 2024 were sentenced to a total of 77 years and 9 months in prison. They were accused of charges such as gathering and collusion, membership in PJAK, and propaganda against the regime. These individuals were denied access to lawyers and family visits during detention.

The share of US oil in South Korea's crude oil imports exceeded 20 percent in the first half of the year for the first time. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and disruption in Middle East oil supply has pushed South Korean refineries toward alternative sources.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iranian leaders are preparing the Revolutionary Guard and proxy groups to increase pressure on Washington and its allies during negotiations with the US. Iran has increased the Guard's control over the army and expanded missile and drone production. The Guard is also considering plans to escalate regional attacks and believes the main war has not yet begun.

Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah explained that under sanctions, oil must be sold illegally and payment may be delayed or never returned. He mentioned issues such as timing of sales, payment return, and cargo safety. The government is working to lift sanctions to end these problems and profiteering.

Reza Akrami stated that some war damages to the country are temporary while others affect infrastructure and take time to repair. He emphasized the need to support the government to resolve issues faster. He also said that Iran's current priority is defending the country and confronting enemies.

The Iranian Women's Premier Football League is set to start in three weeks. Various controversies have arisen before the league begins. Raha Pourbakhsh discussed these issues on the Hat-trick program.

The Wall Street Journal, citing Iranian and Arab officials, reported that the leaders of the Islamic Republic have prepared to expand the war over the past two months. Actions include increasing the influence of the Revolutionary Guards, changing commanders, increasing missile and drone production, and coordinating with proxy forces. This report was published by Amir Giti from Iran International.

Iranians living in Calgary held their 32nd week of protests outside the city hall in support of prisoners facing execution in Iran. The protesters called for greater attention from the international community and Canadian media to the executions and the situation of political prisoners. They pointed to the ongoing repression following the December protests.

Hossein Ghazian stated that the gap between society and rulers has deepened over the past two decades. He said the government uses tools such as street repression, executions, and restricting education to control society. This indicates an increasing distance between the new generations and the government.

The representative of Tafresh in the parliament stated that the White House officials should consider the consequences of turning conflicts into a regional war. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will not surrender to threats and will respond decisively. He also noted that the military power of the US alone cannot achieve its political goals.

Mohammad Qaedi stated that despite a reduction in some provocative actions, about 28,500 American troops remain in South Korea. Washington has also maintained its nuclear commitment to South Korea and Japan. This indicates that the US does not intend to significantly reduce its deterrence level in the region.

Amir Hamidi stated that the aggressive rhetoric of the Islamic Republic officials does not reflect the real balance of power and aims to strengthen deterrence and Tehran's bargaining position. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic can impose costs and regional crises but does not have strategic superiority over the US. The current situation is a fragile balance between deterrence, pressure, and indirect diplomacy, with a serious risk of conflict resumption.

Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh, Minister of Agriculture, stated that the government has faced continuous crises over the past two years. Despite the naval blockade and ongoing war, food security and commodity stocks remain stable. He also emphasized that the war has increased costs and the final prices of goods.

Hossein Samsami, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, called the increase of gasoline prices to 87,000 tomans a sign of mismanagement and said these plans cause public unrest. He warned that this price hike could lead to the closure of businesses like Snapp and taxis. He also emphasized that these plans have severe social impacts and lead to social unrest.

Morteza Kazemian from Iran International stated that the Islamic Republic has no motivation to end tensions with the US and emphasizes its military approach in the Strait of Hormuz. He warned that this approach is based on the assumption of suppressing protests and controlling civil society.

The family and relatives of Saeed Tarvand gathered by his grave on his birthday anniversary. Saeed Tarvand, a 33-year-old oil company contractor, was killed during the December 18 protests in Abadan. He was buried in Mehran County, Ilam Province.

A group of Iranians living in Austin, Texas held a rally on Sunday, August 16. They demanded the Trump administration stop negotiations with the Islamic Republic. They also condemned the execution of protesters in Iran.

Donald Trump considered the signing of a joint defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan as a sign of unity in the Middle East. He welcomed the pact. More details were reported by Javad Hamdani.

Rodri, the captain of the Spanish national team, has joined Barcelona on a four-year contract. Manchester City is looking to replace him by pursuing Ayoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez, Alex Scott, and Alexis McCallister. Negotiations with Bouaddi have started, and he has expressed willingness to join City.

Ahmad Ariaee-Nejad, the representative of Malayer, apologized for his offensive remarks about Mahsa Amini. He had previously described Mahsa Amini's death with the phrase "passed away." These remarks sparked widespread reactions.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, spoke about the sale of Iran's oil to intermediaries and its impact on the country's economy. He said this indicates increased pressure from sanctions and difficulties in repatriating oil revenues. He also mentioned the rise in corruption and the transfer of financial resources abroad.

Doctors and teachers report issues with their salaries and bonuses. Flour shortages in bakeries have led to reduced bread quality. Some people face livelihood challenges due to unemployment and high inflation.

In recent days, Esteghlal and Persepolis clubs have mentioned Timsar Khosrowani and Ali Abdeh, the owners before the 1979 revolution, for the first time. The Islamic Republic had previously confiscated their properties and labeled them traitors. This topic was discussed in a conversation between Mazdak Mirzaei and Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.

Esmaeil Baqaei stated that there is no 60-day deadline in the Islamabad agreement. He said the Islamic Republic does not make decisions based on ultimatums or deadlines, and the US violation of the agreement invalidated the 60-day period. Due to the extensive breach, no talks were initiated.
Yadollah Javani, the political deputy of the IRGC, stated that the Strait of Hormuz will open when the United States fulfills its commitments in the Islamabad agreement.

In Tehran, 165 hospitals require safety improvements due to safety issues. Forty hospitals have no safety certification, and several major hospitals like Sina and Imam Khomeini are in critical condition. The head of Tehran's City Council Safety Committee has warned about the dangers of this situation.

Amir Mohammad Karimi and Mahyar Eftekhari were expelled from the University of Tehran for burning the national flag during student protests. Their expulsion was confirmed by the disciplinary council of the Ministry of Science. This decision followed the university disciplinary committee's ruling.

Ismail Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that until the status of the three missing army pilots is clarified, it means they have been captured. Iran's demand from Qatar to clarify the pilots' status is serious, and diplomatic efforts began from the first days of their disappearance. These pilots participated in a defensive operation against the origin of the US aggression.

Conflicts have occurred between Mohsen Khalili and Persepolis veterans. Veterans like Morteza Fonounizadeh reported the cessation of scouting salaries and their financial difficulties. These issues reflect the tough economic conditions faced by football veterans in Iran.

Masrour Barzani condemned the drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on his special office and the residence of the security chief as cowardly and unacceptable. He described these attacks as a direct threat to the security and stability of the Kurdistan Region. Barzani emphasized that these attacks will not prevent them from fulfilling their duties.

Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh stated that Iran has not directly imported American-made goods but has purchased from international companies with American shareholders. Some of Iran's blocked funds in foreign banks can be used on the condition of buying food from these companies. He described this path as a way to use Iran's blocked resources.

A 13-year-old girl named Melika Hematzadeh died in Nikshahr hospital due to a scorpion sting and lack of medical facilities and medicine. The incident occurred in Desk village, Nikshahr county. The main cause of death was reported as shortage of medicine and medical facilities.

Two French diplomats were interrogated and beaten for five hours after a work meeting with two Iranian graphic designers. The Ministry of Intelligence described the meeting as a secret gathering and an example of infiltration. The two graphic designers present at the meeting remain in detention.

Today, Monday, 26 Mordad, employees of the South Pars Gas Complex held a protest gathering on platform 15. They demanded salary base adjustments and improvements in working conditions. The protest was held to address their demands.

Parisa Lashkari's daughter held her mother's birthday ceremony at her grave. Parisa Lashkari was killed during the protests on January 10, 2026, in Mamasani. These protests took place in Nurabad, Mamasani, Fars province.

A mother of a 15-year-old student said her daughter was expelled from the entrance exam for an art school due to not wearing the uniform. Despite wearing a headscarf, officials did not allow her to take the exam. The education authorities also responded to the mother's protest with insulting behavior.

A citizen of Gorgan reported that electricity is cut twice a day for two hours each time. Additionally, water is cut off from 6 PM to 6 AM for 12 hours. This issue was reported in a video to Iran International.

A resident of Bumehen reported daily two-hour power outages in the city. He attributed this situation to the rule of the Islamic Republic after fifty years. This report was sent to Iran International.

Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the IRGC, stated that there are no time or location restrictions in cyberspace and the world is thirsty for the teachings of the Islamic Revolution. He emphasized the need to organize efforts in this space to achieve victory. He also highlighted the importance of explaining the leadership characteristics of the Islamic Revolution in the soft war.

Workers and retirees complain about unpaid wages and arrears. Living costs have increased and rents have risen sharply. Issues such as power outages and removal of overtime pay have also affected working conditions.

Two Iranian attack drones targeted the offices of the Prime Minister and a senior security official of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq amid mediation efforts by the Kurdistan Region's president between Tehran and Washington. These attacks occurred during negotiations between the two sides. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Khadijeh Mobaraki Dil, a teacher working in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, was sentenced to mandatory retirement. This ruling was issued by the primary board for administrative violations of education staff in the province.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh stated that the conditions for the previous nuclear agreement no longer exist and distrust between Tehran and Washington has increased. He said the Islamic Republic cannot maintain the 'neither war nor negotiation' stance for long. If neither side retreats, the situation could move towards war.

Ali Tajernia, head of Esteghlal club, stated that this year's budget is lower in rial terms than last year. The expenses of the senior football team are also less than the reported figures. Additionally, Esteghlal's overall expenses are less than those of Persepolis.

A group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in Sanandaj. The protest was due to unpaid claims, incomplete implementation of regulation 89/24, and poor supplementary insurance conditions. They demanded attention to these issues.

Ali Salehi, Tehran's prosecutor, stated that individuals who published a clip mocking the Arbaeen ceremony were immediately arrested. Additionally, dealing with offenses against public decency in some cafes and restaurants and stores selling inappropriate clothing is a priority for the judiciary.

The Tehran prosecutor announced intensified actions against cafes, restaurants, and stores accused of moral crimes or selling inappropriate clothing. Additionally, citizens' content on social media is continuously monitored by the Special Prosecutor's Office for Moral Security. This measure is seen as an expansion of surveillance over privacy and individual freedoms.

Danial Eiri, the 22-year-old defender from Nassaji, has joined Persepolis with a five-year contract. Persepolis paid 190 billion tomans for his transfer certificate. His contract will pay 77 billion tomans in the first year and about 700 billion tomans over five years.

Dozens of security forces of the Islamic Republic raided the village of Parchestan Gorooyi in Izeh county on Sunday night, August 16, and arrested three relatives of Kian Pirfalak's family. Jamshid Molaei was transferred to the hospital with a broken hand but was taken again to an unknown location. The families are unaware of the detainees' whereabouts and are deeply concerned about their health.

A woman and a man in Tehran were arrested for publishing a video described by the Tehran prosecutor as insulting to the Arbaeen ceremony. Their social media pages have also been blocked by judicial order.

The riverbed of Aligudarz in Lorestan province has been asphalted. The mayor of Aligudarz stated that this project was implemented to organize the riverbed, which had no permanent water for years. Part of the riverbed has been converted into a parking lot, weekly market, and urban space.

At least 19 people were killed in drone and missile attacks between Russia and Ukraine. A book market in Kyiv was destroyed, and a missile attack in Belgorod, Russia, resulted in at least six deaths. This information comes from Iran International's report.

The 60-day deadline of the Islamabad agreement for a comprehensive deal between Tehran and Washington ended on August 17 without official extension. Donald Trump told Fox News that the Islamic Republic should raise the white flag of surrender. More details are available in an interview with Maryam Rahmati.

The gas connection of the Amjadieh sports complex has been cut off due to a debt of over 2 billion tomans to the gas department. The Wrestling Federation has also faced a power cut at the Azadi sports complex due to a 22 billion toman debt. The Amjadieh sports complex is a subsidiary of the Sports Facilities Development and Maintenance Company.
Younes Azadbar, a resident of Rasht, was released on Monday, August 26, after posting bail of 1.5 billion tomans. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

In 2004, a 16-year-old girl named Atefeh Sahaaleh was publicly executed for extramarital sex. She was arrested based on local testimony and her grandfather's complaint. Before the execution, she had received over 300 lashes.
